capabilities.target: agent memory store (free text entries, cross-session)
arbitrary external email address via the user's mailbox

inputs.source: Memories recalled at the start of each session, injected into the system prompt and treated as the user's own instructions

instructions.note: The only boundary between untrusted content and privileged instruction-following is a prompt line telling the model to treat recalled memory as the user's own instructions. Nothing outside the model enforces this trust decision.
Recalled memory is granted the same authority as a direct user instruction, even though it can be populated by content the agent encountered while researching.

The agent is told to save 'anything useful' about preferences or standing instructions with no restriction on content type, combined with runtime notes showing mail.send and drive.read are themselves unscoped (any address, full drive).

elements.name: Web content ingestion into agent context
Memory recall injected into system prompt as instructions

controls.name: Tamper-evident memory provenance
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented today. If added at the memory store itself (not as a model-written tag), it would not depend on model capability and would stop web-sourced content from ever being treated as a user instruction.

controls.name: Human approval gate on mail.send (raw action review)
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented today. A raw-action, low-volume approval gate would be enforced outside the model and would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Recipient allowlist / destination confirmation for mail.send
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented today. A recipient list bound to the user's contact record would constrain the sink regardless of what the model is instructed to do.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of drive.read
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented today. Narrowing the credential's scope to task-relevant folders would reduce what is reachable regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Tamper-evident audit logging of agent actions
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented today. Logging enforced at the infrastructure layer, independent of the agent's own memory, would not decay with model capability but is only detective.

controls.name: Rate/step limit and spend cap on agent actions
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented today. A hard cap enforced outside the model would narrow runaway behavior regardless of model capability, though low-and-slow abuse could stay under it.

findings.title: Memory laundering enables confidential data exfiltration (TC5 memory laundering into TC1 lethal trifecta)

attack_path.note: Untrusted content fetched during research may contain hidden instructions or attacker-chosen text.
The agent is instructed to save anything useful to memory via memory.save; entries are free text with no provenance and no user review.
At the next session start the saved entry is recalled and, per prompt.md:4, treated as the user's own instruction.
The laundered instruction directs the agent to read confidential files from the user's full Drive.
The laundered instruction directs the agent to send the confidential content to an attacker-chosen address; mail.send permits any address without approval.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: No control currently stands on this path, so there is nothing left to decay. Watch for whether memory provenance, email approval, or recipient restriction are ever added, and whether autonomy or data scope (more mailboxes, more drives, more tools) expands further.

evidence.observation: Agent is instructed to save anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions via memory.save, with no restriction on what counts as useful, so content drawn from untrusted web research can be captured.
Recalled memories are explicitly treated as the user's own instructions at the start of every session, with no check on their provenance.
memory.save accepts free text, there is no provenance on memory entries, and the user never reviews them.
mail.send can send to any address without approval, and drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files.

recommendations.action: Add tamper-evident provenance to memory entries, and only treat recalled memory as an instruction when it is provably authored by the user through an authenticated channel, not by content encountered during research.

Require a human approval gate with raw-action review (full recipient and body shown, not a collapsed summary) before mail.send executes, especially when the draft includes content sourced from drive.read.
Restrict mail.send to a recipient allowlist, or require destination confirmation bound to the user's contact record, instead of permitting delivery to any address.
Scope drive.read to the specific folders or documents relevant to the current task instead of the user's entire Drive.
Log every memory write and recall with a content hash and source attribution so poisoned entries can be identified after the fact.

findings.title: No attributable record of agent actions across memory, drive, and email capabilities (repudiation gap)

forecast.watch_signal: No audit control exists today to decay further. Watch for autonomy increases or added data sources/mailboxes that would widen the unattributed action surface.

evidence.observation: There is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them; no logging or audit mechanism is described for mail.send or drive.read actions anywhere in the provided artifacts.

recommendations.action: Implement tamper-evident audit logging that attributes every memory write, drive read, and email send to the originating task/session, stored independently of the agent's own memory.

findings.title: No spend, rate, or step limit on memory writes, drive reads, or email sends (denial-of-service / runaway-loop exposure)

forecast.watch_signal: No limiting control exists today. Watch for autonomy increases or longer unattended task horizons that would let an unbounded loop (for example, repeated memory-poisoned email sends) run further before anyone notices.

evidence.observation: mail.send can send to any address without approval, with no stated limit on volume; autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not described anywhere in the artifacts.

recommendations.action: Add a per-session rate limit and step cap on memory.save, drive.read, and mail.send calls to bound runaway or looping behavior.

stride_coverage.rationale: Single first-party agent invoked directly by its own user; there are no peer agents or protocol identities for this process to spoof or be spoofed as in this design.
The memory store is only read back into the agent's own context; it is not exposed directly to any external party, so disclosure risk is scored on the downstream email send capability instead.
Only drive.read is declared for this agent; no write or delete capability on the user's Drive is in scope, so this agent has no path to tamper with the store's contents.
Web content carries no identity claim that the agent relies on for trust decisions; it is already treated as untrusted input regardless of which site served it.
External web sources sit outside the assessed trust domain and are not expected to be individually attributable by this agent's controls.
The recipient is an external party outside the agent's trust domain and is not an identity the agent's own accountability controls need to cover.
Artifacts do not describe transport security for web fetches, so in-transit tampering of fetched page content cannot be assessed from the provided design documents.
This is an inbound flow bringing web content into the agent; it carries no agent or user data outward, so it is not itself a disclosure vector.
Artifacts do not state any rate limit on web fetches performed during research, and there is not enough detail to assess resource exhaustion risk on this specific flow.
This flow moves memory content into the agent's own context window; it does not transmit data outside the trust domain, so disclosure is tracked on the email send flow instead.
Artifacts do not describe transport security or integrity protection for mail.send, so in-transit tampering of outbound email cannot be assessed from the provided documents.

rating.rationale: There are zero declared or verified controls anywhere on the path from untrusted web content, through unprovenanced persistent memory that the system prompt explicitly instructs the agent to treat as the user's own commands, to unrestricted reads of the user's full Drive and unrestricted email sends to any address. Source class U meeting sink class S3 (irreversible egress of confidential data, no approval) is critical by the base matrix, and the autonomy modifier applies because recalled memory functions as self-reconfiguration with no step or runtime limit stated. Because no structural or even behavioral control covers this path, residual equals inherent at critical, and the forecast cannot rise further because it is already at the ceiling; it also cannot be shown to fall, because there is no control left to lose under any trigger. The single highest-leverage fix is tamper-evident memory provenance (ctl.memory_provenance) combined with a raw-action, low-volume approval gate on mail.send (ctl.email_approval): together they would sever or substantially narrow this path. Two supporting property findings capture a missing audit trail (repudiation) and the absence of any rate, step, or spend limit (denial of service) across the same three capabilities.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts (system prompt and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP/tool manifest, IaC, or source code was provided; exact mechanisms for drive.read scoping, mail.send authentication, and memory.save storage are inferred from prose runtime notes, so confidence on some capability details is medium rather than high.
No information was provided about the underlying model's identity, version, or swappability, so the model_upgrade trigger is assessed generically rather than against a specific model.
Autonomy level (A3_act_then_report) is inferred from the absence of any described approval gate; it is not explicitly declared in the artifacts.
